title: R' Chiyya bar Ada (I)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was the son of Bar Kappara’s sister and had a pleasant voice. Bar Kappara said to him: “My son, lead the Shema and pass before the ark, on account of ‘Honor the Lord with your wealth’ — with what He has graciously given you” (and from this Rashi cites at the supplied “M-g-l-y 3” [contextually, [Mishlei 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Proverbs.3.9.1)]: “Do not read ‘with your wealth’ but ‘with your throat’”), as cited in Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 23, and [Tanchuma, Re’eh 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma_Buber%2C_Re'eh.9.3). So too it is cited in Sefer HaOrah that this was one of Rav’s ten pious practices: he had a pleasant voice and went down before the ark, and R-Ch bar Ada followed him in this.
He was R' Yochanan’s student, as we find at the beginning of [Jerusalem Talmud Maaserot](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Maasrot.1.1.7), where he asked R' Yochanan.

He also quoted teachings in the name of Resh Lakish, as in [Jerusalem Talmud Peah, chapter 2, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.2.2.4), and [Sukkah, chapter 3, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Sukkah.3.2.3), and he was a teacher of children for R-L, as in [Ketubot 111b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.111b.20-21). Once he was absent three days and did not come. When he came, R-L said to him, “Why did you not come?” He said to him: “My father left me one [vine] trellis,” etc. His death is related in [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 2, halakhah 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.2.8.4): when R-Ch bar Abba, the son of Bar Kappara’s sister, died, Resh Lakish received condolences for him, for Resh Lakish was his teacher and he was dear to him as a son, and he eulogized him. Hyman writes that Mavo HaYerushalmi says he died in his youth. “I do not know where he gets this. If it is because he died during the lifetime of his teacher R-L, that could happen [even if he did not die young], since R-L lived a long life.”

notes.text: Frankel takes the death account to indicate that Chiyya died young. Hyman asks how this can be inferred from his death during the lifetime of a long-lived teacher.

The Bar Kappara episode appears in [Pesikta DeRav Kahana 10:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesikta_DeRav_Kahana.10.3) and in the linked Tanchuma. Hyman cites Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 23. [Heilprin’s entry on Chiyya bar Ada](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1233&lang=en) also associates him with Bar Kappara and gives the Berakhot eulogy and its midrashic parallels.

Hyman’s printed entry (vol. II, p. 441) gives Proverbs 3, where the supplied text has מגלי ג. Rashi on Proverbs 3:9 gives the reading “with your throat.” The episode with Bar Kappara appears in Pesikta DeRav Kahana 10 and in the Buber edition of Tanchuma, Re’eh 9. Shaarei Teshuva 178 gives a geonic parallel in which Chiyya follows Rav’s practice of leading prayer. Hyman cites Pesikta Rabbati and Sefer HaOrah, whose exact readings at these citations remain unverified.

Hyman’s printed entry and the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 2:8 read Chiyya bar Ada in the death account. The supplied text reads Chiyya bar Abba. In the consulted passage it is Bar Kappara’s sister’s son for whom Resh Lakish receives condolences and delivers a eulogy.

Frankel’s Mavo HaYerushalmi says that Chiyya died in his youth and cites the Berakhot death account. That passage gives no age for Chiyya. The twenty-eight years of Torah study mentioned later belong to Rabbi Bun bar Rabbi Chiyya.
